messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: Critical — API Gateway (edge) 502/504 spike detected for service redwood-core. Trigger: error_rate > 3% for 3m across eu-west. Pager: george-oncall

george-oncall: I'm on it. Seeing a sudden jump in 502s from front-proxy pool f-proxy-eu-2. Rolling back recent edge config? No deploys in last hour.

alice.sre: Jump looks correlated with an increase in upstream timeouts to runtime-pool-3, TLS handshake errors in logs. Collecting traces. @hector-noc can you validate edge health?

hector-noc: Confirmed: a subset (~12%) of f-proxy-eu-2 instances reporting `upstream reset` and `504 gateway timeout` in the last 10m. Network flaps observed between eu-west-a/b. No infra deploys.

bob-runtime: Checking model-serving nodes (runtime-pool-3). I'm seeing TCP retran spikes and CPU soft lock in one node group. Could be kernel NIC driver flipping MTU with jumbo frames. Pinging infra team.

carla-platform: No maintenance windows. I pushed a small eBPF probe last night but only to staging. Not in prod. I'll list recent config changes: `edge-routes v12` rolled out 3h ago (only header rewrite).

emily-support: Support ping — a customer on eu-west (Acme Corp) reports increased API errors since ~09:10 UTC, they saw `502` on bulk requests. Visible customer impact: degraded, not complete outage.

george-oncall: Triage plan: 1) Isolate failing proxy instances and switch traffic to standby nodes 2) If upstream timeouts persist, instantiate fallback route to cached model variant 3) Notify CS + customers. Starting step 1 now.

alice.sre: Running quick script to mark f-proxy-eu-2 instances as draining:```bash
for id in $(aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:pool,Values=f-proxy-eu-2" --query "Reservations[*].Instances[*].InstanceId" --output text); do
  aws elb deregister-instances-from-load-balancer --instance-id $id --load-balancer-name edge-eu
done
```

bob-runtime: While draining, I'm spinning up 4 extra runtime nodes in pool-4 and adding to router. Also enabling increased keepalive and bumping upstream timeout from 10s -> 20s as a short-term mitigation. Applying patch to proxy config now.

carla-platform: Applied route change: `edge-route: prefer=standby, timeout=20s, circuit_breaker=20%`. Pushed to edge control plane.

george-oncall: After drain and route change: error rate dropped from 4.8% -> 1.2% in 3 minutes. Still seeing periodic 502s, but traffic is stable. Rolling back not recommended yet.

dinesh-eng: Root-cause hypothesis: an intermittent kernel NIC firmware + MTU mismatch causing TCP fragmentation and upstream connection resets under heavy POST body load. Correlates with bulk request patterns from a few major customers. Planning firmware pin on affected hosts.

emily-support: Notifying affected customers: Acme, BetaFin, and GammaApps — sending interim status with mitigation steps. ETA for full remediation?

frank-custsuccess: Please include note about fallbacks — we routed to cached model variant which may return slightly older embeddings. Will that be okay for SLAs?

bob-runtime: Confirmed: cached model variant returns within latency SLO but has small accuracy delta. We'll log `fallback=true` in response headers so customers can detect degraded quality.

hector-noc: Network team scheduled firmware pin and MTU revert on the three suspect hosts in eu-west-a0 at 09:45 UTC. We'll patch in a rolling manner to avoid simultaneous impact.

george-oncall: Current status: incident in "mitigated (partial)". Actions: - keep extra runtime nodes up for 2h - complete firmware pin by 10:15 UTC - retain circuit breaker at 20% for 30m - prepare postmortem once stable.

alice.sre: Saving logs and traces: running `nginx -T` snapshots, tcpdump on affected hosts, and `traceroute` probes to runtime nodes. Uploading artifacts to incident S3: s3://redwood-incidents/3172500042/artifacts/

incident-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-3172500042. Pager cleared.

emily-support: Customer update posted to ACME via private channel + support ticket updated with `investigating -> degraded -> mitigation in place`.

frank-custsuccess: I'll monitor NPS for these accounts and prep proactive outreach.

carla-platform: Note for postmortem: evaluate adding automated probe for MTU/fragmentation mismatch and better circuit-breaker tuning for bulk POSTs.

george-oncall: Thanks team. I'll wait for firmware pin confirmation and then start containment->postmortem transition. Leaving channel open for 30m of stabilization. :thumbsup:
